lines.li: [us] Which road brought you here?
[them] The long one, past three waystations and a toll I won't name.
[us] Is it safe?
[them] Safe enough with guards, and the league keeps plenty of those.
[them] The league keeps a book of everyone who deals fairly with it.
[us] Are we in it?
[them,likesus] You are, and in good ink.
[them,!likesus] Not yet, but there's room on the page.
[us] What is it like at {TOWN}?
[them] A yard full of carts, beasts and strangers, and a waymaster who knows them all.
[us] It sounds busy.
[them] It's the road's own house, so it's always busy.
[us] What do you do at {TOWN}?
[them] I keep the ward, mostly: the beds, the linen and the night watch.
[us] That sounds like hard work.
[them] Someone has to sit up with the sick, and I would rather it was me.
[them] You're the one who doctors here, aren't you?
[us] I do what I can.
[them] Then come to the sickhouse one day and see how the order does it.
[us] I might, at that.
[us] Why does the order take in anyone at all?
[them] Because the sick don't get to choose where they fall ill.
[us] Even your enemies?
[them] Someone lying on a sickbed is nobody's enemy.
[us] Where does the herd go next?
[them,winter] Down to the valleys, where the snow lies thin.
[them,summer] Up to the high grass, until the frost turns us back.
[them] Wherever the grass is, that's where the herd goes.
[us] And you go with it.
[them] We always have.
[them] You keep beasts here, I saw them on the way in.
[us] A few.
[them] Count them at dusk, every night, and you'll never lose one.
[us] Every night?
[them] Every night, and twice when the wind's up.
[us] Is {TOWN} far from here?
[them] It's wherever the camp was pitched last, and that changes.
[us] How do you find it again?
[them] Follow the bells, and the smoke from the roof rings.
